Q: Cannot connect to SQL Server 2019 using new MSOLEDBSQL A:

I had the same error connecting to Azure SQL Server using C++.

Check your connection string.

DRIVER={ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server};Server=${HOST},${PORT};DATABASE=${DATABASE};UID=${USER};PWD=${PASSWORD};Authentication=SqlPassword;Encrypt=No

I had to turn off Encryption for SqlPassword authentication to work.

Then use the SQL_DRIVER_COMPLETE flag and not SQL_DRIVER_NOPROMPT as advised in the Official Documentation here.

SQLDriverConnect(hDbc, nullptr, connStr, SQL_NTS, nullptr,
                                                            0, nullptr, SQL_DRIVER_COMPLETE);

Q: How to disable new 'modal window' in VSCode A:

To disable this, you need to toggle a specific setting in your settings.json or the Settings UI.The FixOpen Settings (Ctrl + ,).Search for: workbench.editor.openSettingsInEditor (or workbench.settings.editor).Ensure it is set to ui or json (the default "editor" mode).However, if you are referring to the Floating/Centered layout that appeared in recent updates, add/change this in your settings.json:

"workbench.editor.showTabs": "multiple",
"workbench.settings.useSplitJSON": false

Q: What permission do I need for /storage? A:

If you need to let the user pick a specific folder on any drive (including those blocked by the File API), the Storage Access Framework (SAF) with Intent.ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE is the only 100% guaranteed way to get access across all Android versions.

Q: MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission request doesn't show A:

The reason you aren't seeing a dialog is that MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is a special app access permission, not a standard runtime permission. Therefore it cannot be granted via the usual requestPermissions() dialog. You must use an Intent to send the user to the specific system settings page:

if (!Environment.isExternalStorageManager()) {
    val intent = Intent(Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION)
    intent.data = Uri.parse("package:$packageName")
    startActivity(intent)
}

Because your app is for private use only, this is the correct way to bypass in Android 11+.

Q: Pass data to parent in layout phase A:

How would the parent know about its children's content? Yes, you could theoretically just try to flatten your whole layout and do all the positioning and stuff on one layer, but that would make horrible and unreadable code and would completely destroy the meaning of having a layout tree in the first place. If I want to bypass everything I'm working with, I could also just render all the pixels myself.

Q: What is THE way of dealing with integer kinds in Fortan? A:

If you're interfacing with C, use the kinds defined in ISO_C_BINDING. For more on the general topic, see my old post https://stevelionel.com/drfortran/2017/03/27/doctor-fortran-in-it-takes-all-kinds/
